newsitem.title: USA: Great Western, Washington Mutual get SEC approval.
newsitem.headline: Great Western, Washington Mutual get SEC approval.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc. Tuesday scored a victory against rival bidder H.F. Ahmanson and Co. in the bitter battle to acquire California thrift Great Western Financial Corp.

Seattle-based Washington Mutual and Great Western Tuesday said the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) declared effective the registration statement relating to their $6.5 billion merger agreement and the two set June 13 for shareholder meetings to vote on the deal.
"The SEC approval certainly helps them going forward ...," said Jim Bradshaw, analyst with Pacific Crest Securities.
Great Western agreed to merge with Washington Mutual in early March to thwart a hostile bid by rival California thrift H.F. Ahmanson and Co.

"The outcome is still up in the air, but Washington Mutual is starting to gain momentum. The differential in prices is pretty even and Washington Mutual has the vote on its agenda," Bradshaw said. "Unless Ahmanson will raise the offer or gain momentum on its exchange offer, I think they'll lose."
Ahmanson Tuesday asked the Delaware Chancery Court for an injunction to block Great Western shareholders from voting on the Washington Mutual merger on June 13.

Ahmanson has been trying to delay a shareholder vote on Washington Mutual's proposal to give the Great Western board a chance to hear from any new boardmembers that are elected at Great Western's annual meeting on June 13.
Ahmanson is seeking to have three directors elected to the board.

Under Ahmanson's proposal, it would swap up to 1.20 shares of its stock for each Great Western share. On Monday, Ahmanson said it was proceeding to file with the SEC relating to its offer and would begin the exchange offer as soon as it is declared effective.
Under Washington Mutual's deal, Washington Mutual would exchange 0.9 of its shares for each Great Western share.
Based on Tuesday's prices, Washington Mutual's bid was valued at $47.08 a share and Ahmanson's bid was valued at about $48 a share.
While Ahmanson's bid still held a premium, some analysts felt Washington Mutual could win the battle because of the friendly nature of its agreement with Great Western.
Washington Mutual executives met Tuesday with analysts in what was described by some analysts as a bullish meeting.
"It looks like their revenues expecations and cost savings expectations are going to be stronger than expected," said one analyst.
